11. After analyzing the relevant provisions of the D.V. Act, it is culled out that the complainant can get relief under the said Act only when she qualifies to be a aggrieved person.
The expression "aggrieved person" means a woman who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the respondent and has been subjected to any act of domestic violence by the respondent.

The expression "domestic relationship"
means a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time,
lived together in a shared household.

The relationship may be by : (i) consanguinity,
(ii) marriage or, (iii) through a relationship in the nature of a marriage, (iv) adoption or, (v) are family members living together as a joint family.
The expression "domestic relationship" is a comprehensive as well as expansive one.

If aggrieved person is living or at any point of time lived together in "shared household" with the person against whom allegations of domestic violence have been made, the Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.9 of 18 provisions of D.V. Act woul

It is relevant to note the expression "marriage" also encompasses "relationship in the nature of marriage".
12.

For seeking relief under the D.V. Act, in the case of relationship in the nature of marriage, the pre condition is that the allegation of domestic violence must relate to the period of subsistence of relationship in the nature of marriage.

The complainant and the respondent started residing at B- 55, Mange Ram Park, Budh Vihar, Phase-I, Delhi-86.
A girl child was borne out of the said wedlock on 18.12.2010.

The relationship by way of marriage or Relationship in the nature of marriage :-
20.
The factum of marriage has been categorically denied by the respondent.
The D.V. Act has to be interpreted in a manner to effectuate the very purpose and object of the Act.
For seeking relief under the D.V. Act, the complainant can not be expected to strictly prove all the ingredients of marriage.
Any other interpretation would defeat the Mahesh Kashyap vs. Renu Page no.14 of 18 purpose of the Act.

The complainant has brought on record the Birth Certificate of her minor daughter as Ex.CW1/G wherein the name of the father has been mentioned as 'Mahesh Kashyap' and the address has been mentioned as B-55, Mange Ram Park, Delhi.
This is the same address on which the complainant has alleged that they lived as husband and wife.

Even otherwise, the complainant can seek relief under the D.V. Act if she is able to establish that the relationship between the complainant and the respondent was in the nature of marriage.
21.
